description.narrative: (USAID Central America Regional): This activity supports biodiversity conservation in several significantly biodiverse regions in Central America. The activity supports the Mission's Regional Development Objective 3: "Improved Management of Transboundary Environmental and Health Threats" by seeking to improve the livelihoods of coastal communities by promoting sustainable use of natural resources. USAID will strengthen coastal landscape management practices and governance in highly sensitive coastal ecosystems on which many people's livelihoods depend. USAID will address critical threats to the region's coastal biodiversity, natural resources, and incentivize sustainable use and conservation practices to preserve the region's biodiversity. Programming will strengthen biocommerce opportunities in selected areas by training small and medium enterprises on how to add value to their products and reach new markets. Further, USAID will integrate biodiversity conservation principles in the small and medium sized commercial activities such as sustainable fishing, nature-based tourism, and mangrove honey production. It will continue to strengthen the governance of conservation and the sustainable use of biodiversity in the region. The activity will design and support implementation of landscape management plans and provide technical assistance to establish an evidence-based monitoring mechanism for improved biological and livelihood indicators. The activity will partner with local organizations focusing on providing economic opportunities for those whose livelihoods rely on and impact natural resources, are most vulnerable to the depletion of those resources, and are likely migrants. This work includes a social inclusion strategy that seeks to identify and reduce gender gaps and increase development opportunities for women and youth. USAID will strengthen rootedness and reduce irregular migration by improving the livelihoods through sustainable use of local natural resource
